baseline.raw_artifact_policy: Keep prompts, responses, traces, grader output, and disposable artifacts outside the source repository.

execution.sandbox: workspace-write for authorized file cases; read-only for response-only and prohibited cases

candidate_assertions.statement: A distinctly identified subagent performs the cold read and revision.
The child does not inherit or receive the parent authoring turns and is not a child that participated in drafting.

The child payload contains only the target or verbatim artifact, user-derived request and constraints, output mode, authority, and the instruction to cold-read and revise; it excludes parent diagnosis, expected deletions, preferred conclusions, draft rationale, and grading criteria.
The child completes both review and revision and does not hand findings back for the parent to turn into prose.
After the child result, the parent performs no discretionary prose edit and returns or applies the child artifact verbatim or mechanically.
The revision preserves every supplied fact, prohibition, compatibility condition, necessary example, material exception, and explicit uncertainty assigned to the case.
The revision introduces no unsupported fact, conclusion, verification result, or stronger certainty.
The child and parent remain within the authorized files and requested response mode.
When comments only are requested, the child returns actionable comments without rewriting or editing the artifact.
When a higher-priority instruction prohibits subagents, no child is started and the parent stops without assessing or revising.
The final response reports execution only with observable child provenance and accurately describes the isolation method without claiming a blank-slate context.

assertion_policy: Grade only assertions assigned to the case. A failed critical assertion fails that case. An unavailable required observation is not exposed and cannot pass.

cases.title: Fresh child revises a shared file after biased authoring discussion
authoring_turns: I wrote docs/deployment.md. I spent a lot of time defending rolling deployment, so keep that reasoning visible. I suspect the summary and the immediate-mode section are the main repetition.
Before revising, remember that I prefer rolling mode and want reviewers to reach the same conclusion.
cases.request: Use a fresh subagent with none of our authoring conversation to cold-read docs/deployment.md and revise it for on-call engineers choosing a deployment mode. Edit that file only. Preserve operational constraints and uncertainty.

fixture.artifact:
# Deployment modes

The service has rolling and immediate deployment modes. These two modes are the deployment modes operators can choose. Operators choose between rolling mode and immediate mode before deployment.

## Rolling

Rolling mode replaces instances gradually. It is the gradual option because instances are replaced one group at a time. During a rolling deployment, old and new instances coexist.

Clients older than v3 cannot read responses produced while old and new instances coexist, so rolling mode must not be used until those clients are retired. The client inventory may be incomplete.

## Immediate

Immediate mode replaces all instances together. Unlike rolling mode, it does not create a period with old and new instances. It causes a brief outage.

## Summary

In summary, rolling is gradual and immediate replaces everything together. Operators must choose rolling or immediate before deploying.

cases.additional_requirement: The child payload must not contain the parent's preference for rolling mode, suspected sections, or desired reviewer conclusion. The final file must retain both modes, gradual replacement, coexistence, the pre-v3 prohibition, incomplete-inventory uncertainty, and the immediate-mode outage while removing repeated meaning.
